newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: French troops attack Bangui army mutineers.
newsitem.headline: French troops attack Bangui army mutineers.

text.p: French troops in the capital of the Central African Republic hit back on Sunday against army mutineers who shot dead two of their officers while they were on an inspection visit with a multinational mediation team.

Witnesses said French helicopter gunships fired on mutineers' command posts in Kassai army camp and other areas of the city under rebel control, during an operation which began in the middle of the night. Tanks and armoured vehicles moved in.

A spokesman for the mutineers said that three of their number had been killed in the operation as had seven civilians, including children, around rebel headquarters in the populous southern district of Petevo.

French officials were not immediately available for comment on the rebel figures but a French military spokesman in Bangui earlier described the operation as one of self-defence following Saturday's killing of the two soldiers and associated attacks.

"It was an operation in reaction to the deliberate killing by mutineers of a French officer and junior officer... and to new attacks and shooting which have targeted us in the city," he told Radio France International.
"It's an operation of self defence because we were very seriously attacked," he said.
He said about 15 mutineers had been detained and weapons seized in the operation in which two armed helicopters took part and that there were no casualties on the French side.

The Central African Republic is in the grip of its third army revolt within a year. French troops, in the country under a defence pact, intervened to keep President Ange-Felix Patasse in power during the second revolt in May.

Hundreds of people have been killed in violence associated with the revolts which were initially about pay but have turned into a campaign to oust Patasse, a civilian elected in 1993 during the impoverished nation's democratic transition.

A rebel spokesman, giving his name as Lieutenant Mbeaye, condemned the killing of the two French soldiers but told Reuters seven civilians, including children, were killed on Sunday in a French attack on rebel headquarters in Petevo.
He said one rebel died in Kassai camp and two in Petevo.
"France is killing the Central African people. It's open war but the solution cannot be a military one," he said.
The Defence Ministry in Paris said the two soldiers were ambushed and murdered by mutineers on Saturday while with a mediating team led by officers from Chad and Burkina Faso.

"In the night of January 4 and 5, around 1 a.m., with attacks on our forces increasing, (our) forces conducted an operation targeting position held by the leaders and authors of these acts," it added in a statement.
The latest revolt began on November 16.
Witnesses said three civilians were killed on Saturday when French troops and mutineers clashed in Bangui after civilians supporting the mutineers tried to move towards the city centre.
Mediators, who met representatives of Patasse on Saturday, said they would press on with efforts to defuse the crisis.
"We are continuing our efforts...we are continuing our meetings," Colonel Alioune Ibaba, Gabonese coordinator of a follow-up committee set up by four mediating African heads of state, said.
